name: Mavacamten
route_note: oral capsule once daily, titrated by echocardiographic LVOT gradient and ejection fraction

discovery.note: Found by screening for compounds that reduce actin-activated myosin ATPase; BMS acquired MyoKardia in 2020.

rx_status: prescription (restricted REMS programme in the US)
tagline: First-in-class cardiac myosin inhibitor for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
summary: Mavacamten is a first-in-class allosteric inhibitor of cardiac myosin that reduces excessive contractility in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. In symptomatic obstructive HCM it lowers the outflow-tract gradient and improves symptoms and exercise capacity, but requires echocardiographic monitoring because it can reduce ejection fraction.
mechanism: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is often caused by sarcomere mutations that increase the number of myosin heads available to bind actin, producing hypercontractility and impaired relaxation.

Mavacamten binds β-cardiac myosin and inhibits its ATPase, stabilising an energy-sparing 'super-relaxed' state and reducing actin–myosin cross-bridge formation. This lowers contractility, relieves left ventricular outflow obstruction and improves filling pressures.
uses: Symptomatic NYHA class II–III obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in adults

history.title: Mechanism published
history.detail: Preclinical work in Science shows a small-molecule myosin inhibitor suppresses HCM development in mice.

history.title: EXPLORER-HCM
history.detail: Mavacamten improves exercise capacity, LVOT gradient and symptoms in obstructive HCM.

history.title: BMS acquisition
history.detail: Bristol Myers Squibb acquires MyoKardia for about $13.1 billion.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US with a boxed warning and REMS; VALOR-HCM shows reduced need for septal reduction therapy.

history.title: ODYSSEY-HCM
history.detail: A trial in non-obstructive HCM does not meet its primary endpoints.

pk.half_life: ~6–9 days (CYP2C19 normal metabolisers); ~23 days in poor metabolisers

serious: Heart failure due to systolic dysfunction (reduced LVEF)
Interactions with CYP2C19/CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers
safety.boxed_warning: Risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction: echocardiographic LVEF assessment is required before and during treatment; certain CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers are contraindicated; available only through a REMS programme.

facts: It can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives.

references.title: Olivotto I et al. Mavacamten for treatment of symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (EXPLORER-HCM). Lancet 2020
